prompt:
Write 11 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1093; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- Nobody gave the claimant's name at the scene; the claimant joined the claim days later.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim received on a rear-end collision report from the insured's vehicle. The claimant reports neck strain and is not represented by counsel at this stage.

Entry 2: Reviewed the insured's policy and confirmed the driver involved is named on the policy. Coverage was in force at the time of loss, and nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the policy start.

Entry 3: Spoke with the claimant, who described the impact and the resulting neck discomfort. The account matched what was recorded at first notice.

Entry 4: Received the photographs from the scene. They confirm the general location and rear-end contact, though some details are not fully visible in the images.

Entry 5: No independent witnesses were identified. The claimant did not provide the other party's details at the scene, and the claimant joined the claim several days after the collision.

Entry 6: Requested prior medical records. No earlier injury to the same body area is known from the information gathered so far.

Entry 7: Reviewed the treatment notes. The injury is consistent with the type and force of the collision, and the treatment followed a typical course.

Entry 8: Inspected the vehicle. A few older scratches were noted that may predate this collision, so the scope of damage attributable to this impact is still being evaluated.

Entry 9: Called the claimant again to go over the account. The claimant gave the same description of events as in earlier conversations.

Entry 10: Treatment has tapered as the claimant improved, consistent with the expected recovery pattern. Reserves were reviewed against the current status.

Entry 11: Claim remains open pending the completion of the damage assessment and a final review of the medical records.
